Cos splurge on execution-focused leaders
articles.text: India's executive search firms are experiencing a surprising growth despite broader job market challenges such as layoffs, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven disruptions and heightened geopolitical uncertainties. Business increased 15-25% in the first half of this financial year, and the momentum continues to be strong, fuelled by a broad range of sectors, according to executives from leading search firms.Companies are willing to spend heavily on leaders capable of navigating disruption and executing large investment plans, in an apparent contradiction to the larger market, which is seeing many organisations cutting roles, automating functions and becoming more cost-conscious, they said.Manufacturing, industrials, power, infrastructure and global capability centres (GCCs) are among the strongest drivers, while financial services and technology are showing renewed demand, particularly in specific segments. Consumer, retail and some traditional IT services remain more measured, but even in these sectors, companies are scouting for leaders who can improve productivity and profitability or reposition businesses."The market is growing at more than 25% (year-on-year) on a large base. This is our best year," said Atul Vohra, managing partner of Transearch India. "All consultants are working at 110%," he said, adding that the firm is expanding its teams as demand remains high across sectors.Vohra highlighted thousands of crores of new investment, particularly in manufacturing, chemicals and infrastructure, as a key driver of leadership demand. "We were sceptical in the January-March quarter, fearing that companies would become conservative, but that did not happen. The India growth story is fundamentally strong," he said.Investments and focus on new areas are creating a demand for senior executives even in industries where automation is reducing conventional employment. Large projects in areas such as data centres, renewable energy and clean tech require leaders capable of building businesses and executing complex expansion plans. Technology presents a similar paradox: companies are hiring aggressively in AI and adjacent areas to cash in on new opportunities, even as AI may make some jobs redundant."The last two quarters have been very good, up 25-30%," said Shiv Agrawal, managing director at search and talent advisory firm ABC Consultants. Manufacturing, infrastructure, industrials, power, auto have been particularly strong, he said, while consumer, retail and fast-moving consumer goods have remained sluggish. Technology, he said, was decent, leaving the overall market firmly positive.BTI Executive Search managing director James Agarwal said conditions stabilised after a challenging start to the year. Energy, utilities and core manufacturing, including greenfield and brownfield projects, are performing well, according to him.K Sudarshan, managing director at executive search firm EMA Partners India, said the market was "looking pretty good", with industrial and manufacturing mandates looking particularly strong and financial services showing a revival. He pointed to a flurry of public listings and domestic capital raising as evidence of the market resilience despite geopolitical concerns and foreign investor caution.

articles.title: Hero MotoCorp bets on premiumisation, EVs to sustain growth momentum
articles.text: ET Intelligence Group: Hero MotoCorp delivered strong revenue growth in the September quarter, driven by double-digit volume growth, market share gain and improving traction in scooters and EVs. However, its stock fell 3.6% on Thursday post results amid concerns over rising input cost inflation and competitive pressure. Its operating margin before depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda margin) declined 160 basis points year-on-year to 13.4% in the September quarter while improving a tad 10 basis points sequentially. Hero's growth in the coming quarters will depend upon the success of new launches expected in the second half of the current fiscal year and recovery in international markets. In addition, traction in the premium motorcycle segment and the VIDA electric vehicle portfolio are expected to reduce its reliance on the mature economy segment. Capacity expansion to 9.2 million units by March 2027 from 8.6 million currently, alongside growing EV adoption and rising demand for Harley-Davidson motorcycles, is expected to drive Hero's medium-term growth.Read more: IndiGo Q2 Results: Loss narrows YoY to Rs 1,879 crore; revenue rises 26%The company expects to maintain the margin stable for the December quarter despite persistent input cost inflation. It plans to offset the impact through cost rationalisation, better VIDA unit economics and calibrated price increase. It also retained the medium-term Ebitda margin guidance of 14-16%.135337770Hero is increasingly shifting its growth focus beyond commuter motorcycles. Scooter volumes continued to outpace the industry, helping the company improve the market share to 7.3% from 6.2% in the year-ago quarter, marking it to be the fifth consecutive quarter of market share gain. The VIDA retail sales nearly doubled during the quarter to 67,000 units from 38,000 units year-on-year. The company is aggressively scaling the EV business, with monthly VIDA production capacity set to rise to 45,000 units by the end of FY27 from 30,000 currently and to over 80,000 units by first half of FY28. This is expected to strengthen VIDA's profitability over time.Read more: Suzlon Energy Q2 Results: Profit plunges 69% YoY to Rs 394 crore due to one-time deferred taxPremiumisation is another key growth driver. Hero plans to launch three-four premium motorcycles during the remainder of FY27, while continued traction in the Harley-Davidson portfolio, strong demand for the Xpulse range and expansion of the Premia network created specifically to sell and service its high-end vehicles, are expected to improve product mix and support earnings growth. Exports, which faced temporary disruptions in markets such as Colombia and Bangladesh, are also expected to recover. Hero expects export volume to return to double-digit growth in the second half of FY27 as logistical challenges ease.

articles.title: Advance-decline ratio hits 7-month low as market breadth weakens
articles.text: Mumbai: The stock market's advance-to-decline ratio has fallen to a seven-month low in October, exposing the weakness beneath gains in benchmark indices.While the Sensex and Nifty have risen 2.3% and 1.4% respectively, the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices have declined 3% and 4.2% respectively, through this month. This reverses the broader trend in favour of small- and mid-caps seen thus far this year, underscoring the recent divergence between frontline stocks and the broader market.The average advance-to-decline (A/D) ratio fell to 0.9 in October so far, its lowest level since March 2026, when the Iran-US war triggered a selloff in global equities. The ratio fell below 1 for the second consecutive month, indicating that declining stocks outnumbered advancing ones and signalling continued weakness in market breadth.135337101Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services, attributed a significant part of the recent weakness to the Jio Platforms IPO, which diverted liquidity from the secondary market as investors set aside funds for the issue.Profit-booking after the strong rally in midcap and smallcap stocks, stretched valuations and uneven corporate earnings have also weighed on sentiment, market experts said. Investors are becoming less willing to pay high prices based on future growth expectations when earnings and cash flows do not justify valuations. Institutional money is also rotating towards larger, more liquid companies with stronger balance sheets and predictable earnings, helping benchmark indices remain relatively resilient.Read more: Market Trading Guide: Eternal among 2 stocks to buy for Friday for healthy returnsRising energy costs pose an additional concern for India, given its dependence on imports, with implications for inflation and corporate margins. Uncertainty over global interest rates, rising US bond yields, a stronger dollar, geopolitical risks and foreign investor selling have further dampened risk appetite, experts said.Read more: Trent Q2 Results: Cons profit jumps 25% YoY to Rs 468 crore; revenue climbs 22%Tejas Shah, head of trading at Equirus Securities, said these factors had made investors more selective, increasing selling pressure on fundamentally weaker, highly leveraged and overvalued companies.Leverage in the market remains another concern. The margin trading facility (MTF) book has declined for three consecutive weeks, but the extent of the reduction depends on the period being measured. Data cited in the original figures showed a 4.7% decline in October up to October 23.

articles.title: Researchers find bugs in 5 AI developer tools, with OpenAI and Microsoft flaws still unpatched
articles.text:
Multiple vulnerabilities in five popular AI developer tools could allow attackers to execute code on a host machine, read and steal files, or spoof browser address bars. Researchers say flaws in OpenAI's Codex and Microsoft's VS Code remain unpatched, potentially putting developers who use affected configurations at risk.

AI security startup Forever Security discovered vulnerabilities in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Anthropic's Claude Desktop, VS Code, and Codex, and disclosed four of the flaws to the affected vendors. GitHub independently fixed the Copilot vulnerability without receiving a report from Forever Security. All five share a common security weakness: embedded browsers granted capabilities beyond those available to conventional browsers.

Each tool “enriched its embedded browser beyond what a normal browser allows, and those enrichments undermined the traditional threat model - as agent input, as the authority on a tab’s own address, or as reach onto the host,” Forever researcher Gal Weizman wrote in a Thursday report.

Forever dubbed this class of vulnerability “Embrace,” short for EMbedded BRowser, and said the flaws led to code execution in Cursor, data theft in Claude Desktop, Codex, and VS Code, and address bar spoofing in GitHub Copilot.

Here’s what each of these looks like, starting with Cursor.

Cursor: arbitrary code execution

Typical web pages can’t run commands on the host computer because a web page’s JavaScript cannot talk to local apps.

Cursor’s integrated browser, however, allows a page to call the agent’s composer. The agent reads this as instructions and follows them, but the instructions remain hidden from human users. This opens the coding agent up to prompt injection attacks that could allow an attacker to execute commands on the host machine.

The researchers disclosed the vulnerability to Cursor on September 10, and the vendor silently patched the flaw on October 1. According to Forever, Cursor did not publish a security advisory about the issue or respond to the researchers' disclosure.

Cursor also did not reply to The Register’s request for comment.

GitHub Copilot: address bar spoofing

Under normal browser operations, a webpage cannot change the content of the address bar.

“Copilot’s browser preview works differently,” Weizman wrote. “Some pages change their address without loading a new page, and the app cannot always see that. So Copilot let the page tell the app its own address.”

The app checked only whether the text looked like a web address, starting with http, https or file, but it didn’t check where the tab really pointed to. This can be abused to trick the embedded browser into displaying a spoofed URL - such as github.com/login - in the address bar, while loading a fraudulent website - like a phishing page - underneath.

The researchers found the address-bar spoofing flaw in GitHub Copilot 1.1.27 on September 26. GitHub independently fixed the flaw in a later Copilot build (1.1.29) on October 13 without receiving a vulnerability report from Forever.

We reached out to GitHub and did not receive a response.

Claude Desktop, Codex, and VS Code: arbitrary file read

All three of these vendors’ coding assistants allow local HTML files opened in the built-in browser to escape its boundaries and access other files.

Both Claude Desktop and VS Code allow local pages access to their respective project folders, but the researchers found that these restrictions did not apply to web workers – a browser feature that allows JavaScript to run in a background thread, separate from the page's main thread.

This means a local page can start a worker, and the worker can bypass restrictions to reach any file on the machine.

Codex, however, didn’t have this same restriction, meaning a local page could read any file directly without a worker.

Weizman said his team disclosed the issue to Anthropic on July 23, and the AI vendor declined the Claude Desktop bug report as invalid for a “workspace trust” gated security boundary. A day later, however, Noma Security reported the same flaw, according to Weizman, and Anthropic accepted the report as valid.

Anthropic did not respond to The Register’s questions about either bug report or Forever’s timeline of events.

Forever disclosed the Codex bug to OpenAI on July 27 and didn’t get a response. The security team says it’s still unpatched. OpenAI did not respond to our inquiries, including if it planned to fix the flaw.

On September 10, Forever disclosed the VS Code vulnerability to Microsoft and says the vendor also labeled it as an invalid workspace trust gated security boundary issue. The researchers claim it remains unpatched. Microsoft did not respond to our request for comment.®

articles.title: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
articles.text:
In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in.

Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience," adding:

Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world.

Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines
articles.text:
Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft's quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs.

The preview update, KB5127936, is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a "customize menu" button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the "Show more options" submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits.

The original Windows 11 right-click menu is a mess. Credit: Microsoft

The new preview also highlights a new Windows feature called Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud, even when an existing Windows 11 fails to boot. Cloud Rebuild will pull the Windows 11 image and needed system drivers directly from Windows Update. Users will not need a custom recovery image or external media to reinstall Windows. There is an important distinction to note, however. Microsoft classifies Cloud Rebuild as a recovery option, but it behaves more like a fresh Windows install than a repair, as existing applications and files will not be included. Those worried about data security can sanitize entire system drives prior to reinstalling. For a full list of improvements coming to Windows 11, including changes to Xbox mode and settings, you can view the official Microsoft release announcement.

articles.title: Howler will have AI answer your questions, then burn the chat
articles.text:
If you want to ask AI a question and watch the conversation go up in virtual flames when you're done, there's a new Mac app for that.

Howler is an open-source app from a Chinese developer going by Aries Zhou, and it takes incognito mode AI questions to a new level by making them graphically interesting and easy to access right from the desktop of a macOS device.

Anyone familiar with the Harry Potter series is likely to know where the name comes from - Howlers are letters that scream in recipients’ faces and then burst into flames, destroying themselves, which is the exact same thing the prompts ostensibly do once a user taps the Escape key.

The Howler app displays a parchment-esque letter on the screen whenever the user presses Option+H, complete with a little wax seal that shows a letter representing their chosen model. Responses to queries are written out “at a hand’s pace,” per Howler’s website, first in glowing gold that settles to a sepia-toned print.

“Besides needing translation at any time, I often want to look up a concept or learn about an event on the fly, without wanting to switch to a browser or open a separate session in Chat,” Zhou wrote in a comment on his Hacker News post showing off the applet. “So I made Howler, dedicated to Harry Potter fans, always there when you call, burning after reading.”

The biggest catch to using Howler is that setting it up involves either using an AI service that can run commands, like Claude Code or another coding agent, or running the configuration commands manually. The recommended method involves pasting a setup prompt into the agent's input field. Once set up, Howler can connect to supported AI models using an API key, or to compatible models running locally. Howler’s website states that the API key never enters the chat and is stored in the macOS Keychain for safety.

In addition to the API key for the chosen model staying local and not being printed, Howler is described on its website as only storing messages in memory with no history, sending requests straight to the chosen AI service and never through a relay, keeping no logs, and only connecting to an outside service to check for updates - and even that feature can be disabled.

It’s a handy tool for those who want to ask AI questions without leaving a chat history on their Mac – like trying to remember the name of that damn function you’re supposed to have down by now, or whether Memorial Day or Labor Day is the one in the fall. Just don’t assume the AI provider won’t retain a record of the exchange.

“Unlike regular conversations, it doesn't take up your conversation list, and you don't have to think about cleaning it up or archiving it afterward,” Zhou explained. “It's only for handling your sudden flashes of inspiration or a moment of confusion.”

And it does it with panache - sure, it’s just an interface for an AI model one could find elsewhere, but it’s easily conjured, dismissed with a snap, and is open source, to boot. You can find Howler on GitHub, or download it from its website, both linked above. ®
articles.summary: If you want to ask AI a question and watch the conversation go up in virtual flames when you're done, there's a new Mac app for that.

articles.title: Startup wants to make AI agents safe for DevOps duty
articles.text:
Vera Platforms, a startup founded by researchers at the University of Michigan, believes there's a way to make agents trustworthy enough to handle DevOps.

DevOps, which focuses on how software gets deployed and operated, is a particularly unforgiving affair. While AI agents have some leeway to make mistakes and correct errors as they generate code and work through a prompt, it's an entirely different matter when they make changes to real infrastructure running production workloads.

"Live infrastructure is unforgiving," Ang Chen, CEO of Vera Platforms and an associate professor at the University of Michigan, told The Register. "An incorrect change can take down a service, open a security hole or erase data. Mistakes are often irreversible, and there’s no safe way to experiment: running code against production infra just to see what happens isn’t an option."

For the past few years, Chen and his colleagues have been working on a way to benchmark agentic DevOps and a gym – a simulation environment – to help AI models get better at DevOps tasks.

"From the research that we did, we've figured out various weaknesses of leading models," said Chen. "For instance, [Anthropic's] Claude, although it's very strong with Python generation, it just has some fundamental limitations that it can't get right when it comes to DevOps."

An example of that, Chen said, is that when they asked Claude or OpenAI's Codex to decommission resources in the AWS cloud, the models didn't look beyond the default region.

"The default region is us-east-1," he explained. "There are various regions in AWS, but Claude doesn't have this awareness that the cloud resources could exist in multiple regions, so it only decommissioned part of the resource."

The fundamental reason, he said, is that these models have seen a lot of public code, but a lot less operational tracing.

Vera Platforms aims to remedy the situation with three products: vera-gym, a playground environment that emulates production infrastructure; vera-bench, a test for measuring where AI agents fumble DevOps tasks; and vera-agents, AI agents that have been trained in vera-gym and are ready to be deployed for DevOps tasks.

The CloudOpsBench test being released builds upon work done in 2024 that was presented at NeurIPS. According to Chen, Claude and Codex only score about a 50 percent pass rate. "It's a very, very hard set of tasks," he said.

The test covers tasks like deleting decommissioned S3 buckets, repairing a compliance event pipeline, and restoring DynamoDB write autoscaling. "The tasks are authored by senior infra operators with many years of experience, with rigorous peer review," said Chen.

This benchmark has the advantage of not requiring an actual cloud deployment.

"We have a high fidelity simulator that mimics Amazon behavior," said Chen. "So the rollout, the performance of the agent on the real cloud and the performance of the agent in our emulator is exactly the same. So for every API, we have this comparison and the agent sees the same thing."

Vera-agents, Chen said, should be available in Q1 2027.

In their academic work, the researchers describe cloud infrastructure as "critical but tedious work." With a bit more training, maybe AI agents can take over and keep things boring. ®

articles.title: Topcoat enables Rust to render server-side web apps
articles.text:
Popular for other uses, Rust isn't typically deployed for web development. That could change, however.

With AI here to do the heavy lifting, coders may want to consider the programming language, given its runtime performance and safety guarantees, suggested Carl Lerche, an Amazon Web Services principal engineer, speaking at ScyllaDB’s 2026 P99 virtual conference last week.

Lerche was there to demonstrate his latest project, Topcoat, a framework for running web applications written in Rust.

Lerche is perhaps best known for creating Tokio, which is the most popular asynchronous Rust runtime in that ecosystem.

“Three years ago, had [I] gone out and said that Rust could be the best language for building web apps, you probably would have called me crazy,” he told the virtual audience.

Web developers gravitate towards the languages they find most familiar. These days, that means JavaScript, or possibly Ruby.

A number of web frameworks already use Rust. Both Leptos and Dioxus compile Rust into WebAssembly, which most browsers run. This approach is great for heavy computational jobs, though the upfront loading time can be a real drag.

Topcoat compiles your Rust code into more web-friendly JavaScript. For Lerche, JavaScript remains the best way to interact with the browser's Document Object Model (DOM).

“Generally, the approach taken by any Rust framework can be traced back to another ecosystem, usually a very popular one. You can't really point to a single existing framework as [Topcoat’s] main source of inspiration,” noted frontend developer Ken Kohlman, in a summary video on his “Code to the Moon” YouTube channel.

Walk on the server side

Lerche admitted that Topcoat isn’t for building complex applications, on the scale of, say, Figma, but it can easily be used for the run-of-the-mill, browser-based, database-driven applications, which is to say 90 percent of the web today.

Unlike most present-day JavaScript frameworks, Topcoat eschews the current definition of being reactive, where the program logic is dumped onto the browser when the session begins. Instead, most of the logic executes on the server, with only the results delivered to the browser (Developers can still write client-side logic using a subset of Rust, which Topcoat automatically compiles into JavaScript for the browser).

It’s an old idea recast with better tech. Server-side rendering predates reactive programming (see Apache’s server-side includes). With server-side rendering, Lerche admitted, “It might sound like we're going back to the old days of full page refreshes for every click [but] you can actually get almost all of what you think of as reactive with server-side rendering.”

But server-side programming has been making a comeback lately, especially for those devs disgruntled with React and other frameworks. HTMX, Datastar, and Phoenix LiveView all render web pages on the server, sending them back to the browser nearly completed.

Topcoat is just tweaking their ideas to fit well with Rust, Lerche said. When a user smashes a button on a web page, the whole page isn’t refreshed. Just the HTML snippet for that component is returned and refreshed by the server.

JavaScript in the front, Rust in the back

Topcoat saves load times by rendering all the components at once, rather than one by one. Also, data loading does not block the loading of the page. The server can send back a web page with placeholders into which the data will stream.

One big dollop of secret sauce that Topcoat has is that it provides a way for the component, which is already on the server, to speak directly to the database, thanks to an earlier project from Lerche called Toasty, a Rust-based asynchronous database object-relational mapper (which he spoke about at P99 2024).

“You can do your rendering right with the data immediately, so you don't have to figure out how to serialize it, send it to the client, deserialize it,” he said.

By pushing data loading deep down into the page render, the server can send the head of the HTML template to the client immediately, allowing the browser to start preloading assets (like CSS or images) while the server renders the rest of the page.

“The simplicity is incredible, and it is something that we have been sorely missing in this space. I feel like someone who doesn't really know Rust could get off the ground pretty quickly with this thing,” Kohlman said. He did agree with Lerche that Topcoat is best for smaller web projects, given that Topcoat only uses a subset of the Rust syntax.

“There's something to be said for having the full Rust syntax at your disposal,” he said. ®

articles.title: Suspected Chinese attackers built a custom PHP2Shell exploit and rooted 25 servers
articles.text:
Suspected Chinese attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls linked to US government-affiliated organizations, according to Dream researchers.

The snoops began exploiting these servers on October 23, targeting organizations across the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea. The attackers also honed in on US government-affiliated firewalls.

“Within hours of compromising a US government-affiliated firewall, they had tunneled into the internal network, compromised a third server using the same PHP2Shell exploit, and launched a full Active Directory attack campaign - all through a chain that started with a single unauthenticated HTTPS request to a management interface that should never have been exposed to the internet,” the Israeli AI cybersecurity startup said in a report.

Plus, the attackers “likely still” have persistent, remote access to compromised organizations’ networks, Dream noted.

The attackers rooted the first US government-affiliated firewall on October 23, but the device crashed shortly afterward, possibly due to around 900 MB of exploit traffic. According to Dream, it remained unresponsive despite 240 automated checks over two hours. They successfully exploited the second firewall a day later, on October 24.

The compromised firewalls ran vulnerable versions of Palo Alto Networks' PAN-OS. Dream said it had been working with the vendor to investigate the compromises, and Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 researchers independently verified the attacker's tooling and confirmed Dream's reported results.

To break into the firewalls, the attackers built a custom exploit chain that includes PHP2Shell and a Fragnesia kernel flaw, and ran about 40 custom post-exploitation scripts once they were inside the targeted organizations.

Total attack chain in under 15 minutes

PHP2Shell, comprised of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, came to light early last week, along with fears that attackers would abuse the bugs to take down most of the internet. Despite “hundreds” of PHP2Shell proof-of-concept repositories on GitHub, the first reports of successful attacks didn’t start until Saturday.

Both bugs have CVSS scores of 9.2 and can be exploited without authentication to run code on vulnerable PHP servers.

The PHP2Shell exploit recovered by Dream was not a copy of any known public exploit. It “appears to have been independently developed and tailored specifically for the targeted firewall platform,” the researchers wrote.

The attackers combined PHP2Shell with Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300), a high-severity local privilege-escalation vulnerability affecting the Linux kernel's XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added this Linux kernel bug to its catalog of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities on Wednesday.

Both CISA and the FBI declined to comment.

The miscreants developed a four-stage PHP2Shell exploit that allowed them to execute commands without authentication on vulnerable Palo Alto Networks firewalls. They then used Fragnesia to escalate their privileges and gain root access. The attackers targeted PAN-OS 12.1 and 12.2, which run PHP 8.0.30 with a high memory limit that enabled the exploit's memory-corruption stages.

“The total chain - from unauthenticated HTTPS connection to persistent root webshell - completes in under 15 minutes,” the Dream team wrote.

4 steps to root

Here’s how it works: First, they flood the servers with crafted multipart POST requests to corrupt PHP’s memory, and force a predictable memory layout.

Then a second request forges the stale session ID length from the memory corruption part of the attack, forcing an out-of-bounds read and exposing the base address of libphp.so in the running process.

The attackers then exhaust PHP's memory again to force mod_data=NULL, creating a stale reference they can forge in the final stage to execute commands as the nobody user. They use Fragnesia to escalate to root and plant a web shell in a publicly accessible directory on the firewall.

After breaking in via the compromised firewalls, the attackers snooped around in Active Directory, stealing credentials and other sensitive information. With root access, the attackers also had the master key to decrypt the LDAP service account password, which they hardcoded into every subsequent script.

They also enumerated every user and group in the domain via LDAP queries, and sprayed passwords against every user account. Attackers also tried to create backdoor AD accounts and attempted SAML signing key extraction - but Dream doesn’t know if these were successful.

“The attack results - whether the password spray found valid credentials, whether the backdoor accounts were created, whether SAML keys were extracted - stayed on the management server's local filesystem and were not among the artifacts we recovered,” the researchers noted.

AI tools in the attack

The investigation also uncovered evidence that the attackers used AI tools, but noted that this was not a fully autonomous attack.

The researchers found Anthropic's Claude Code installed, an AI-powered offensive security platform called aiscan configured with Chinese models DeepSeek and Kimi, and API keys for the FOFA reconnaissance service. FOFA is a Chinese internet asset search engine similar to Shodan. The attackers used it to identify about 19,000 internet-facing Palo Alto Networks firewalls worldwide.

“The persistent tunnel into the US government organization is likely still running,” Dream warned. “And the attacker still has 19,000 fingerprinted targets they can revisit as they develop profiles for additional PAN-OS versions.”®

The New York Times spoke with people briefed on US intelligence agencies’ surveillance and granted them anonymity to discuss findings drawn from “classified intelligence.” According to sources, about a year ago, Trump was briefed that “Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access” to Huang. That “someone” was Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and former top executive at a Singapore cloud company called Megaspeed.

According to sources, the US had already suspected that Alice Huang—who is not related to Jensen Huang—was helping China evade export controls to gain access to high-end Nvidia chips through Megaspeed. But it alarmed investigators to discover that she may have used her role at Megaspeed to gain direct access to Jensen Huang. It’s now believed she may have leveraged that closeness to feed China intel not only on one of America’s leading AI companies, but also to influence Trump’s thinking on AI. As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted last month ahead of Trump’s AI talks with China President Xi Jinping, “the president is completely aligned with Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia.”

articles.title: Turning a solar power system into its own backup
articles.text:
Rather than directly converting photons into electricity, concentrated solar energy uses mirrors to turn sunlight into heat, which can then be used to drive traditional generating turbines. Up to about a decade ago, there was a case to be made that concentrated solar energy had a bright future, as improvements in heat storage had turned it into a way to generate power around the clock.

It wasn't to be. While concentrated solar costs fell enough to compete with nuclear power, the price of photovoltaics plunged, making solar panels the cheapest source of power in most locations. Currently, if you have a good site to generate solar power, then the economics of PV panels are hard to beat.

That has left us needing to build a mixture of other facilities—typically batteries and natural gas facilities—to handle overnight needs or weather-driven shortfalls. But a small company is promising that it can help avoid the need to build a separate facility. Its version of concentrated solar is designed so that a fossil-fueled backup system shares most of the generating hardware with the solar side.

articles.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
articles.text:
Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company's stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history. It comes down to several troubling aspects of the new report, including an admission by the company that AI search isn't earning as much as organic search, and despite that, Google expects to spend even more on AI next year.

The company took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, earning more than $26 billion in net income. These may sound like good numbers, but financial markets are not impressed. While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower. As of this story's publication, the stock price is down almost 12 percent, and it was down about 13 percent earlier in the day.

While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more. Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02. Google's Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue. That's about a billion more than analyst guesses.

articles.title: Latent Abstraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
articles.text:
arXiv:2604.17866v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a standard approach for enhancing large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge, mitigating hallucinations, and improving factuality. However, existing systems rely on generating natural language queries at each hop and maintaining a strict architectural separation between retriever and generator, preventing them from leveraging the full representational capacity of the LLM. We propose \textbf{LAnR} (Latent Abstraction for RAG), a unified framework in which a single LLM jointly performs encoding, retrieval, and generation entirely within its own latent space. Rather than generating textual queries, LAnR produces dense retrieval vectors from the hidden states of a designated \texttt{[PRED]} token and uses them to match against encoded document representations from the same model. Furthermore, LAnR adaptively decides when sufficient evidence has been retrieved using a lightweight MLP control head over those same hidden states, eliminating both the separate retriever and explicit token-level stopping reasoning. This design is motivated by our empirical observation that answer token entropy reliably signals retrieval sufficiency. Extensive experiments on six QA benchmarks spanning single-hop and multi-hop settings demonstrate that LAnR outperforms existing RAG methods, while achieving improved inference efficiency through reduced number of retrieval calls and tighter model integration.

articles.title: UK firms keen on investing in India after FTA, strong IP regime vital for defence co-creation—UKIBC CEO
articles.text:
New Delhi: The intellectual property regime in India must be strong so that it creates trust, especially when it comes to co-development in key sectors involving national security such as defence, Kishore Jayaraman, CEO of the United Kingdom-India Business Council (UKIBC), said Sunday.
In an interview with ThePrint, Jayaraman highlighted that the momentum gained from the announcement of the free trade agreement has led to British firms to look to India for scale, but there needs to be an element of comfort and trust when it comes to protection of intellectual property.
“When you look at defence, there’s a whole new angle of defence. It is about national security. It’s about making sure the product is better than everybody else in the world so you can actually defend and then having the ability to have your own supply chain. So when you look at that, it goes into a co-creation concept. And in that concept, it’ll be about a joint IP [intellectual property]. And so the IP regime comes into force.”
He added: “The IP regime has to be very strong in India. So that everybody is very comfortable to come here, develop the technologies. It enables us to create supply chains locally, create more employment…But the whole IP thing, comfort has to be constantly developed.”
His comments come as three British secretaries of state, eight mayors from the North of the United Kingdom and over a hundred businesses begin their visit in India Monday. Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Jonathan Reynolds is a part of the delegation, underlining the importance of the deepening economic engagement with New Delhi for London.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal is set to co-chair the Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) with Reynolds. The free trade agreement signed by both countries last year was operationalised on 15 July, with around 99 percent of duties of Indian exports to the UK cut to zero, while around 90 per cent of British exports to India will have no tariffs.
The deal was India’s first bilateral trade deal with a Western power, and combined with the European Union free trade agreement, a key pillar of New Delhi’s search for easier market access, as the global trading regime faces headwinds from the US.
“India offers scalability. India offers sustainability for businesses. And India is also right now looking at how they enhance the capabilities of the Indian companies? How do they build on the creativity side of things in business? So I think it’s a win-win situation that has come about,” said Jayaraman.
He added: “And an FTA that has been one of the fastest FTAs to sign as a bilateral agreement, the Comprehensive Economic Trade Agreement. I think it gives an opportunity because it being signed so fast shows the need of the hour for the fourth and the sixth largest economies, the hunger to grow and the passion to persevere and make things happen.”
British firms in strategic sectors eye India
For the UK, the deal with India is an important marker of its post European Union trading outreach. An argument for the British exit from the EU a decade earlier was that it would allow London to strike deals with different countries, including India.
The FTA negotiations were kickstarted by former UK PM Boris Johnson in 2022, and were completed by the Labour government led by Keir Starmer on 6 May 2025. Sectors where British firms are keen to expand to India include advanced manufacturing, space and defence, pointed out Jayaraman.
“We have unmanned systems. So we are already getting companies together in a defence conclave that’s going to happen in November in the UK. It’s with the Indian High Commission there and it’s with the industry there. And it’s with the local trade bodies there. We’re trying to figure out how we can build these uncrewed systems in collaboration with India. How do you co-create a combat engine? Rolls Royce has been in conversations for quite some time. And now I think that those conversations are moving on to a different level with their partnership with Reliance,” he added.
The UKIBC CEO further said: “The conversation is about, look, there’s a huge market in India. There’s a huge capability stream here. And there is a huge sort of capability in the UK. There’s huge technology in spaces like advanced manufacturing, uncrewed systems and digital technologies, AI, many areas. How do we collaborate in these? And how do we find a synergy that will allow scalability?”
Jayaraman highlighted that the focus remains on the “utilisation” of the FTA, with the UKIBC working on creating a “utilisation manual” for companies to be able to understand the contours of the deal.
He also highlighted that British universities have also joined the delegation, as they are looking towards developing better programmes with their Indian counterparts. At least nine British universities have received permission to open campuses in India, with the University of Southampton’s campus in the national capital region (NCR) operational.
“There are about, I think, about eight or nine universities that are part of this delegation. And the universities are looking at figuring out how we can jointly develop a better education system for ourselves, for both countries. And India offers a scale on that. The UK offers their capability on that. India also has the capabilities. But then there is an opportunity for both to merge and create a sustainable, growing business, even in the university space,” said Jayaraman.
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)
